name: definition-invalid-tag-group
description: A Definition tag does not appear in a tag group at the top level in an annotation.
common_causes: Definition tag not enclosed in parentheses
Definition appearing in nested groups instead of top-level
Multiple definitions in the same group
Definition mixed with other content improperly
Using curly braces in definitions
explanation: Definitions must appear in their own top-level tag group containing only the Definition tag and a single inner group with the definition's content. They cannot be nested or mixed with other tags at the top level.
correction_strategy: Ensure definitions are properly structured in top-level groups

correction_examples.explanation: Enclosed definition in required parentheses
Removed extra nesting from second definition
Moved all content into the single inner group

correction_patterns: Enclose Definition tag and content in top-level parentheses
Ensure only Definition tag and one inner group in definition group
Remove extra nesting levels
Separate multiple definitions into different top-level groups
Replace curly braces with proper HED syntax
fix_instructions: 1. Identify Definition tags in the annotation
2. Ensure each Definition is in its own top-level group
3. Verify group contains only Definition tag and one inner group
4. Check that Definition doesn't appear in nested groups
5. Separate multiple definitions appropriately
validation_hints: Count parentheses levels to ensure proper nesting
Verify no extra tags alongside Definition in same group
Check that definitions appear only at top level
Ensure inner content is properly grouped

name: definition-invalid-multiple-definition-tags
description: A definition's enclosing tag group contains more than a `Definition` tag and an inner group.
common_causes: Adding extra Definition tags in the same group
Misunderstanding that definitions should contain only one Definition tag
Attempting to define multiple things in one group
Confusion about definition group structure
explanation: Each definition group should contain exactly one Definition tag and its content group. Multiple Definition tags in the same group create structural ambiguity.
correction_strategy: Use separate definition groups for each Definition tag

correction_examples.explanation: Separated multiple definitions into individual groups
Created separate definition groups with appropriate content

correction_patterns: Create separate groups for each Definition tag
Ensure each definition has its own content group
Remove extra Definition tags from single groups
fix_instructions: 1. Identify groups with multiple Definition tags
2. Separate each Definition into its own group
3. Distribute content appropriately between definitions
4. Verify each definition group structure
validation_hints: Count Definition tags per group
Ensure one Definition per group maximum
Check definition content distribution

name: definition-invalid-inner-group-defs
description: A definition's inner tag group contains `Definition`, `Def` or `Def-expand` tags.
common_causes: Nested Definition tags within definition content
Including Def or Def-expand tags inside definition inner groups
Attempting to define definitions within definitions
Confusion about definition content structure
explanation: Definition inner groups should contain only the content being defined, not other definition-related tags. Nested definitions create circular reference issues.
correction_strategy: Remove definition-related tags from inner groups or restructure

correction_examples.explanation: Moved nested Definition to separate top-level definition
Removed Def tag from definition content

correction_patterns: Move nested definitions to top level
Remove Def/Def-expand tags from definition content
Keep definition content simple and non-recursive
fix_instructions: 1. Identify definition-related tags in inner groups
2. Remove or move them to appropriate locations
3. Ensure definition content contains only descriptive tags
4. Verify no circular references exist
validation_hints: Check inner groups for Definition/Def/Def-expand tags
Ensure definition content is purely descriptive
Verify no recursive definition structures

name: definition-invalid-bad-number-of-placeholders
description: A definition that includes a placeholder (`#`) does not have exactly two `#` characters.
common_causes: Unequal number of placeholders in definition and content
Missing placeholder in definition name or content
Extra placeholders beyond the required pair
Misunderstanding placeholder pairing requirements
Incomplete placeholder implementation
explanation: Definitions with placeholders must have exactly two # characters: one in the definition name and one in the content. This creates a proper placeholder substitution pattern.
correction_strategy: Ensure exactly two # characters in definition

correction_examples.explanation: Removed extra placeholder to have exactly two
Added missing placeholder in content

correction_patterns: Count # characters and ensure exactly two total
Add missing # in content if definition name has #
Remove extra # characters beyond the required pair
Verify placeholder pairing consistency
fix_instructions: 1. Count total # characters in definition
2. Ensure definition name has # if using placeholders
3. Add exactly one # in definition content
4. Remove any extra # characters
5. Verify placeholder substitution pattern
validation_hints: Count # characters - should be exactly 2
One # in definition name, one # in content
Remove extra placeholders
Add missing placeholder pairs

name: definition-invalid-placeholder-incorrect-of-positions
description: A definition has placeholders (`#`) in incorrect positions.
common_causes: Placeholder in content without corresponding definition placeholder
Standalone # character not properly positioned
Mismatched placeholder positions in definition structure
Incorrect placeholder syntax usage
Misunderstanding of placeholder positioning rules
explanation: Placeholders must be properly positioned: in definition names they appear as suffix (/Name/#), in content they replace specific values. Incorrect positioning breaks substitution logic.
correction_strategy: Position placeholders correctly in definition structure

correction_examples.explanation: Added placeholder to definition name to match content
Placed placeholder in proper tag position

correction_patterns: Add # to definition name when content has placeholders
Replace standalone # with proper tag/# format
Ensure placeholders appear in valid tag positions
Match definition name and content placeholder usage
fix_instructions: 1. Check if content has # but definition name lacks #
2. Add # suffix to definition name if needed
3. Replace standalone # with proper tag/# format
4. Verify placeholder positioning rules
5. Test placeholder substitution logic
validation_hints: Definition names with placeholders end in /#
Content placeholders appear in tag/# format
No standalone # characters
Match definition and content placeholder usage

name: definition-invalid-placeholder-conflict
description: Definitions of the same name appear with and without a `#`.
common_causes: Mixing placeholder and non-placeholder versions of same definition
Inconsistent definition naming across files
Confusion about when to use placeholders
Copy-paste errors with different placeholder usage
Misunderstanding definition uniqueness requirements
explanation: Each definition name must be used consistently either with or without placeholders. Mixed usage creates ambiguity about which definition applies and breaks substitution logic.
correction_strategy: Use consistent placeholder approach for each definition name

correction_examples.explanation: Made placeholder usage consistent or used different names

correction_examples.wrong: Definition/Event with and without # in same file
correction_examples.correct: Definition/Event consistently without # or Definition/Event/# consistently with #
correction_examples.explanation: Chose one approach and applied consistently

correction_patterns: Choose placeholder or non-placeholder approach per definition
Rename definitions to avoid conflicts
Update all instances to use consistent placeholder usage
Verify definition name uniqueness
fix_instructions: 1. Identify conflicting definition names
2. Decide on placeholder vs non-placeholder approach
3. Update all instances to use consistent approach
4. Or rename one definition to avoid conflict
5. Verify definition consistency across files
validation_hints: Each definition name must be consistently used
Check for same name with/without # conflicts
Verify placeholder usage consistency
Ensure definition name uniqueness

name: definition-invalid-multiple-definitions
description: Definitions with the same name have different contents.
common_causes: Copying a definition into several definition entries and editing one copy
Two sidecars in a dataset defining the same name with different contents
Attempting to override or extend an existing definition under its name
Defining a name once with a placeholder and once without
explanation: A definition name may be defined more than once only when every definition of it is identical (same placeholder form, same contents without regard to case or order). Definitions of the same name whose contents differ are ambiguous: tools cannot tell which to expand.
correction_strategy: Rename a definition that is meant to differ, or make the repeated definitions identical

correction_examples.explanation: Renamed the second definition because its contents differ
An identical repeat of a definition is allowed; only differing contents are an error

correction_patterns: Rename a same-name definition whose contents differ
Make repeated definitions identical when they mean the same thing
Use descriptive suffixes for related but different definitions
fix_instructions: 1. Collect every definition with the repeated name
2. Compare their placeholder forms and contents without regard to case or order
3. Rename the ones that differ, or make them identical
4. Update all Def and Def-expand references to a renamed definition
validation_hints: Report only same-name definitions whose contents differ
Treat identical repeats as one definition
Compare contents across all definition sources of the dataset

name: definition-invalid-content-has-top-level-tag
description: A definition's contents contain, at any level, a structural reserved tag (Definition, Def, Def-expand, Onset, Offset, Inset, Delay, Duration, Event-context; reason d) or a tag with the required or unique attribute (reason j).
common_causes: Using top-level or unique tags within definition content
Including Event-context or other required tags in definitions
Misunderstanding that definitions should contain reusable content
Adding context-specific tags to generic definitions
Confusion about what content is appropriate in definitions
Putting an Onset, Offset, Inset, Delay, or Duration group inside a definition instead of in the annotation that uses it
Referring to another definition with Def inside a definition
explanation: Definition content should contain reusable, generic tags. The structural reserved tags and tags with the required or unique attribute may not appear anywhere in a definition's contents, at any depth: timing tags such as Onset, Delay, and Duration belong in the annotation that uses the definition, and definitions may not refer to other definitions.
correction_strategy: Remove reserved, required, and unique tags from definition content; put timing tags in the annotation that uses the definition

correction_examples.explanation: Removed Event-context which is a required/unique tag
Kept only generic content without context requirements
Write the Duration where the definition is used: (Duration/2 s, (Def/HasDuration, (Blue)))
Write out the tags of the other definition instead of referring to it

correction_patterns: Remove Event-context and similar required tags
Keep only generic, reusable content in definitions
Avoid context-specific or unique tags in definitions
Focus on core descriptive content
fix_instructions: 1. Identify required/unique tags in definition content
2. Remove Event-context and similar tags
3. Keep only generic, reusable tags
4. Verify definition contains appropriate content
5. Test definition reusability
validation_hints: Check for Event-context in definitions
Remove required or unique attribute tags
Keep definition content generic and reusable
Verify appropriate definition content
specification_reference: 3.2.8.1. The Definition tag; Appendix B DEFINITION_INVALID d and j

name: definition-not-allowed-here
description: A definition appears in an unexpected place such as an events file or sidecar.
common_causes: Placing definitions in event annotations instead of definition section
Including definitions in regular HED strings
Misunderstanding that definitions belong in specific sections
Confusion about definition vs definition usage (Def/Name)
Incorrect file structure for definition placement
explanation: Definitions should only appear in designated definition sections or files, not mixed with regular event annotations. Use Def/Name to reference definitions, not Definition tags.
correction_strategy: Move definitions to appropriate sections or use Def references

correction_examples.explanation: Replaced definition declaration with definition reference

correction_examples.correct: Move definition to defs section, use Def/Name in events
correction_examples.explanation: Separated definition declaration from usage

correction_patterns: Move Definition tags to defs section of sidecar
Replace Definition with Def/Name in event annotations
Separate definition declaration from usage
Use proper file structure for definitions
fix_instructions: 1. Identify misplaced Definition tags
2. Move definitions to appropriate defs section
3. Replace Definition usage with Def/Name references
4. Verify proper file structure
5. Test definition references work correctly
validation_hints: Definitions belong in defs sections only
Use Def/Name to reference definitions
Check file structure for proper definition placement
Separate definition declaration from usage

name: definition-invalid-duplicate-definitions-differ
description: A definition name may be defined more than once only when every definition of it is identical; the same name with different contents is an error.
common_causes: Copying a definition into several sidecar entries and editing one copy
Two sidecars in a dataset defining the same name differently
explanation: Identical definitions of one name (the same placeholder form and the same contents, without regard to case or order) are allowed and treated as one definition. Definitions of the same name whose contents differ are ambiguous and are an error.
correction_strategy: Make every definition of a name identical, or rename one of them

correction_examples.explanation: The two definitions now have the same contents; tag order does not matter

correction_patterns: Compare the contents of same-name definitions without regard to case or order
Rename a definition that is meant to differ
fix_instructions: 1. Collect every definition with the repeated name
2. Compare their placeholder forms and contents ignoring tag order and case
3. Make them identical or give one a new name
validation_hints: Report only same-name definitions whose contents differ
Treat identical duplicates as one definition

name: definition-invalid-second-part-not-placeholder
description: The value of a Definition tag has a part after the name other than a single # (reason l): Definition/NewDef/3 and Definition/NewDef/Extra fail. Definition/NewDef/#/# fails too, as reason f (three # in the definition) or l.
common_causes: Writing an example value instead of # after the definition name
Adding a second word to the definition name with a slash instead of a hyphen
Writing # twice after the name
explanation: A Definition tag's value is the definition name, optionally followed by /# when the contents hold one placeholder. Nothing else may follow the name: the value is filled in where the definition is used, as Def/NewDef/3, not where it is defined, and a name may not contain a slash.
correction_strategy: Keep only the name, or the name and a single #, in the Definition tag

correction_examples.explanation: The definition takes #; the value 3 goes in the Def tag, Def/NewDef/3
The name is one nameClass value
Only one # follows the name

specification_reference: 3.2.8.1. The Definition tag; 3.2.8. Reserved tags (value forms table); Appendix B DEFINITION_INVALID f and l

name: definition-invalid-content-has-delay-or-duration-in-8-1-0
description: Delay and Duration may not appear in a definition's contents (reason d). The rule holds in every standard schema version; 8.1.0 is not special, and this case pins it there because the 8.1.0 schema does not mark Delay and Duration reserved.
common_causes: Assuming that because the 8.0.0 and 8.1.0 schemas do not mark Delay and Duration reserved they may be used in definitions
Putting the timing of an event inside the definition that describes it
explanation: The structural reserved tags, Delay and Duration among them, may not appear anywhere in a definition's contents. The rule is applied by tag name in every standard schema version, so it holds under 8.0.0 and 8.1.0 although those schemas do not carry the reserved attribute; timing belongs in the annotation that uses the definition.
correction_strategy: Remove Delay and Duration from the definition and write them in the annotation that uses it

correction_examples.explanation: Write the Duration where the definition is used

specification_reference: 3.2.8.1. The Definition tag; 3.2.8. Reserved tags; Appendix B DEFINITION_INVALID d; Appendix B.3. Differences for earlier schema versions

name: definition-invalid-in-value-entry
description: A sidecar value entry contains a definition.
common_causes: Putting a definition in the HED string of a value column
explanation: Definitions in a sidecar go in a categorical entry whose annotations contain only definitions. A value entry may not contain one. When the value entry also has two placeholders, a validator may report PLACEHOLDER_INVALID instead.
correction_strategy: Move the definition to a categorical entry that holds only definitions

correction_examples.explanation: The definition is in its own categorical entry

correction_patterns: Keep definitions in a definitions-only categorical entry
fix_instructions: 1. Find definitions in value entries
2. Move each to a categorical entry with only definitions
validation_hints: A value entry is a string with one #, not a dictionary

name: definition-invalid-beside-other-tags
description: A sidecar categorical annotation contains a definition and a tag that is not a definition.
common_causes: Adding an ordinary tag to an annotation that holds definitions
explanation: A sidecar annotation that contains a definition must contain only definitions. This holds for each annotation by itself, also when every annotation of the column has a definition. A validator may report the extra tag as TAG_INVALID instead.
correction_strategy: Remove the other tag, or move it to an annotation without definitions

correction_examples.explanation: The annotation holds only the definition

correction_patterns: Check each annotation that has a definition for tags outside definitions
fix_instructions: 1. Find annotations with definitions
2. Remove any top-level tag or group that is not a definition
validation_hints: Every annotation in the failing columns has a definition, so comparing annotations is not enough

name: definition-invalid-identical-in-one-string
description: Identical definitions of one name in the same HED string are one definition, not a repeated expression; the same name with different contents in one string is an error.
common_causes: Pasting the same definition twice into one sidecar entry
Merging two sidecar entries that each carried the same definition
Editing one of two copies of a definition that sit in one string
explanation: Definitions are processed on their own, apart from the annotation they appear in, so identical definitions of one name (the same placeholder form and the same contents, without regard to tag case or order) are one definition even when both copies are in the same HED string. They are not a repeated expression. Repeated Def tags, such as Def/X, Def/X, are still a repeated expression. Two definitions of one name whose contents differ are an error wherever they appear.
correction_strategy: Make the copies of a definition identical, or rename the one that is meant to differ; removing a redundant identical copy is optional

correction_examples.explanation: The two definitions differ, so one of them gets a new name
Identical copies in one string are allowed and treated as one definition

correction_patterns: Compare same-name definitions in one string as you would across entries
Do not report identical Definition groups as repeated expressions
fix_instructions: 1. Find definitions of the same name, including several in one string
2. Compare their placeholder forms and contents ignoring tag order and tag case
3. If they differ, make them identical or rename one
validation_hints: Identical Definition groups in one string are one definition
Def/X, Def/X in one string is still a repeated expression
Definition names are matched without regard to case

name: definition-invalid-name-case
description: Definition names are matched without regard to case, so names that differ only in case name the same definition and must have identical contents.
common_causes: Capitalizing a definition name differently in two sidecar columns
Assuming that X and x are different definition names
explanation: A definition name is treated like a schema node name: it is matched without regard to case. Definition/X and Definition/x define the same name, so they are allowed only when their contents are identical, and are an error when the contents differ.
correction_strategy: Use one spelling for each definition name and keep its definitions identical, or choose a genuinely different name

correction_examples.explanation: X and x are the same name, so the definition meant to differ gets a different name

correction_patterns: Compare definition names case-insensitively
Spell each definition name the same way everywhere
fix_instructions: 1. Fold definition names to one case before comparing them
2. For names that match, compare the contents
3. Rename a definition whose contents are meant to differ
validation_hints: Definition/X and Definition/x name the same definition
Same-name definitions with different contents are an error even when the names differ in case

name: definition-invalid-value-case
description: Tags in definition contents are compared without regard to case but values with case, so definitions of one name that differ in the case of a value are different definitions.
common_causes: Typing a value in different case in two copies of a definition
Assuming the case rule for tags also applies to values
explanation: Two definitions of one name must be identical. Tags are compared without regard to case, so Label and label match, but values keep their case, so Label/abc and Label/ABC are different. (Definition/X, (Label/abc)) and (Definition/X, (Label/ABC)) are therefore different definitions of X, which is an error.
correction_strategy: Make the values in every definition of a name match exactly, including case, or rename one definition

correction_examples.explanation: The value now matches exactly; the case of the tag does not matter

correction_patterns: Compare tags without case and values with case
Copy definitions exactly rather than retyping them
fix_instructions: 1. Collect every definition of the repeated name
2. Compare tags ignoring case and values exactly
3. Make the values match or rename one definition
validation_hints: Label/abc and label/abc are the same tag expression
Label/abc and Label/ABC are different values
